articles.title: Larry Ellison bought eight homes near his Florida mansion, quite purchase made several residents upset, making homeowners association adopt restrictions
articles.summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has quietly acquired eight residential properties inside a single gated Florida development, spending nearly $10 million
articles.body: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has quietly acquired eight residential properties inside a single gated Florida development, spending nearly $10 million to house household staff and private tutors within commuting distance of his primary oceanfront estate, a report has said. The buying spree occurred over a matter of weeks in 2023 across Palm Meadows Estates, a 288-home community in West Boynton Beach located about 30 minutes from Ellison’s landmark Manalapan compound.As per a report by The Wall Street Journal, the acquisition unsettled several neighbours, prompting the community's homeowners association (HOA) to pass formal ownership caps to block single buyers from amassing large property clusters in the future.Larry Ellison’s secret house huntThe acquisition drive started in March 2023 when Palm Meadows resident and LuxeIQ broker Kimmie Cruz was contacted by an outside agent seeking access to local listings for an undisclosed buyer looking to purchase roughly ten homes. The buyers focused on single-story ranch layouts, expanding their interest to properties not listed on the open market. That reportedly prompted Cruz to approach homeowners directly, pitching the opportunity of a verified cash buyer ready to close without standard listing hurdles.The buyer’s identity surfaced shortly after, when the 82-year-old tech billionaire toured the neighbourhood with his personal security guards. An LLC tied to Ellison closed on all eight properties across May and June 2023, spending roughly $10 million, according to county real estate filings cited by the publication.For some residents, the sudden purchases resulted in profits. For example, a family offloaded their three-bedroom, 2,100-square-foot house for $1.2 million – more than double the $567,000 they paid for it in 2019.Housing for tutors and domestic StaffThe Palm Meadows homes stand in contrast to Ellison’s primary residence. While his flagship estate is a palatial trophy property, the Boynton Beach residences are conventional suburban homes with private yards and occasional pools.Sources familiar with the arrangement told The Wall Street Journal that the houses accommodate key staff who manage the billionaire’s daily operations, including educators instructing some of the five children he shares with his wife, Jolin Ellison. At the main Manalapan compound, dedicated spaces are set aside for homeschooling older children, who learn several languages under multiple private instructors.Residents report several staff members drive Tesla vehicles, and municipal records indicate building permits were filed to install Tesla Powerwall energy units across all eight homes following the purchase. (Ellison sat on Tesla’s board of directors from 2018 to 2022.)Limits after community backlashThe concentration of properties under a single corporate owner drew friction from within the gated enclave, which features 24-hour manned gatehouses, a community clubhouse and water views from every lot. Uneasy about having a cluster of staff-occupied houses operated by an outside LLC, community members raised objections.According to Cruz, the Palm Meadows homeowners association enacted new ownership restrictions designed to stop similar bulk purchases.Rising trend of Billionaire staff compoundsEllison’s move highlights a growing pattern among ultra-wealthy executives, hedge fund founders and public figures who purchase off-site residential clusters for domestic employees. High-cost real estate markets make it difficult for essential staff, such as chefs, nannies, security personnel and estate managers, to reside within a practical driving distance.Housing staff in separate suburban quarters allows high-profile employers to maintain personal seclusion at their primary residences.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russia cuts welfare, education and healthcare budget as war spending hits new high
articles.summary: Russia is preparing to cut spending on welfare, education and healthcare in its 2027 federal budget while raising taxes, as the government struggles to
articles.body: Russia is preparing to cut spending on welfare, education and healthcare in its 2027 federal budget while raising taxes, as the government struggles to meet the rising cost of its war in Ukraine, according to fiscal documents reviewed by Reuters.The draft budget proposes 17.1 trillion roubles ($202.58 billion) for defence in 2027. That is about 27% higher than the 13.5 trillion roubles originally allocated for defence and would be the highest military spending level since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.Military spending takes priorityThe increase in defence spending comes as Russia's finances have come under growing pressure during the four-and-a-half-year war. Moscow has used its fiscal reserves, borrowed more money and raised taxes to help finance its expanding military expenditure.The new budget would reduce spending on social policy by 7% from the initial plan. This area covers state pensions, payments to war veterans and maternity benefits.Education spending would fall by 6%, while healthcare funding would be cut by 6.8%.Spending under the "national economy" category, which includes road building, infrastructure projects and subsidies for agriculture and other industries, would also fall by 7.4%.Russia is preparing a three-year budget to improve long-term financial planning, but its budget projections have repeatedly been revised as the war has continued. The government has also missed its annual deficit targets several times.Higher taxes and rising household costsThe pressure on public finances is also being felt through higher taxes and other costs. The 2027 draft budget includes new tax increases, while utility tariffs are also expected to rise by more than previously planned.Those measures have angered some supporters of the Kremlin, particularly after they were announced following this month's parliamentary election.The new State Duma is expected to approve the budget. The pro-Kremlin United Russia party is set to retain a constitutional majority, while Russian authorities have repeatedly said that winning the war in Ukraine takes priority over other spending needs.Debt costs add to the pressureRussia's financial burden is not limited to military spending. The government is also spending more on servicing its debt as high interest rates increase borrowing costs.Debt-servicing costs in 2027 are expected to be 21.6% higher than originally planned. They are projected to account for 9.4% of total government spending next year and could rise further to 10.6% by 2029.The federal budget does not include regional and municipal spending, which also accounts for a significant portion of Russia's social expenditure. Even so, the latest figures show how the prolonged war is forcing Moscow to devote more of its finances to defence while putting pressure on other areas of government spending.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A pro-Al Qaeda publication has called for copycat attacks on US and Israeli airliners, referencing the September 11, 2001, attacks and Wednesday’s
articles.body: A pro-Al Qaeda publication has called for copycat attacks on US and Israeli airliners, referencing the September 11, 2001, attacks and Wednesday’s attempted takeover of a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.The call appeared Friday in the latest edition of al-Bayan, a weekly publication launched in July by supporters of Al Qaeda. The article referred to both the 9/11 attacks and the attempted takeover of Flydubai Flight FZ1073.“The war isn’t over yet — planes carrying Zionists, Americans and all the other infidels fighting against Islam are still hovering in the skies and can be targeted, as happened on September 11th and 30th,” the Arabic-language article said.The article featured an image of a plane crashing into the World Trade Center’s Twin Towers on September 11, 2001, alongside an image referencing Wednesday’s attack on the Flydubai flight.“America and the Zionists have far more enemies today than before,” the article said. “Perhaps a man who does not believe in God will target them and his operation will ultimately benefit Islam.”It added: “The day will come when the empire of evil America will end.”The publication’s Telegram channels appeared to circulate the post on Saturday before it was apparently taken down.The co-pilot suspected in the Flydubai attack has been identified as an Omani national. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Press Club of India has condemned the Delhi Police’s alleged treatment of journalists and imposition of internet ban during protests at
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Press Club of India has condemned the Delhi Police’s alleged treatment of journalists and imposition of internet ban during protests at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Friday and Saturday, saying such behaviour “cannot be normalised in a democracy”.In a statement, the Press Club said it was “shocked and dismayed” by the police action against journalists covering the protests and raised concerns over media freedom in the national capital.“Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues,” the Press Club said, adding that the restrictions on journalists even in the heart of Delhi “do not bode well for the trajectory of media freedom in India”.The Press Club also urged the Delhi Police to immediately act on a complaint filed by a female journalist and ensure that mediapersons are able to perform their duties without facing “aggression and threats”.Complaints trasferred to Crime Branch: PoliceEearlier in the day, Delhi Police said it had received complaints from three female journalists alleging sexual harassment during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3. The complaints have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action, police said.Delhi Police X post reads, "On 03-10-26, during the protest in the New Delhi area, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists in the context of the emergent law and order situation. New Delhi District has received their complaints and the same are transferred to Crime Branch, Kamla Market for further action."Jantar Mantar is witnessing protests demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Around 150 people demanding Kumar's removal were detained in and around Jantar Mantar on Saturday as security forces prevented protesters from gathering at the site.Those detained included senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal, Swaraj India founder Yogendra Yadav and AISA national president Neha Bora.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Painting of Dryburgh bridge found on back of map after 150 years
articles.summary: The watercolour on the back of a map gives a rare snapshot of the Dryburgh suspension bridge shortly after it opened.
articles.body:
A striking watercolour of a bridge in the Scottish Borders, which had gone unnoticed in archives for more than 150 years, has been found by accident on the back of a geological map.

Luis Albornoz-Parra, of the British Geological Survey (BGS), stumbled on the artwork while carrying out research for Historic Environment Scotland (HES) on the building stones of Dryburgh Abbey.

The painting of the Dryburgh Suspension Bridge - on the back of geological field notes - is believed to have been painted by Benjamin Peach while conducting field work in the 1870s.

BGS said the artwork offered a "snapshot of the iconic crossing" and is thought to be from just a year after it opened.

Abbey's Romantic notion over biodiversity

Abbey restrictions lifted after safety checks

Albornoz-Parra was looking through old field slips - the original maps that geologists fill with field observations while mapping the rocks of an area - when he uncovered the painting in the archives at The Lyell Centre in Edinburgh.

"I was charmed by the quality of the watercolour and wanted to share it with my colleagues," he said.

"Mostly I was fascinated by the fact that Peach was an excellent geologist and palaeontologist - his geological studies and theories still stand - but he was also such an excellent artist.

"I can imagine him having a lunchtime break from all the geological mapping, during which he would be drawing the watercolour."

BGS said the work provided a "unique record of the Victorian landscape" around Dryburgh.

It was found while looking through early field slips to gather more information about the area's abbey, which is currently undergoing restoration.

The first bridge at the spot was built in 1817 to replace a ferry, but it lasted only a year before being blown down in a gale.

A replacement lasted a bit longer before it, too, collapsed in stormy weather in 1838.

The third bridge, which is still standing, was completed in 1872 and it is believed to have been captured by Peach's artwork a year later when he was known to be conducting fieldwork in the region.

Daniel Burgess, BGS geological data steward, said: "Field slips have always been a vital tool for geologists since the inception of the survey in the 19th Century, as a way of recording important observations, measurements and notes whilst out in the field.

"It was not unusual for geologists, who are often out in the field for weeks at a time, to sketch the landscapes that have been shaped by the underlying geology.

"In this example, Peach is showing how the tough volcanic rocks of the Eildon Hills dominate the landscape around Dryburgh."

He said that their records did occasionally throw up a "welcome surprise" and they knew "almost instantly" it was one of Peach's artworks.

Peach worked at BGS from 1862 until his retirement in 1905.

Alongside his geological work, he produced hundreds of sketches and paintings during his field surveys.

He also played a pivotal role in resolving the Highlands Controversy - one of the most significant geological debates of the 19th Century about how different layers of rock came to be in their current location.

Peach and others eventually resolved it through fieldwork which showed that older layers or rock had ended up on top of younger strata because of huge thrust faults.

The geological field map is now stored in the BGS archives, alongside approximately 40,000 other items, which include administrative records and the papers of BGS staff.

articles.title: Horniman Museum's new Nature Gallery to open in February
articles.summary: The new Nature Gallery hopes to explore people's connection to and reliance on nature.
articles.body:
The Horniman Museum is set to open its new Nature Gallery in February 2027.

The south-east London museum said the fully refurbished space, previously named the Natural History Gallery, had been reimagined to celebrate the variety of life on earth and explore humankind's place within, and impact on, nature.

The opening is the final part of the museum's £12.5m Nature + Love transformation project, supported by The National Lottery Heritage Fund.

Michael Salter-Church MBE, chairman of the museum, said: "Opening these wonderful new spaces marks the end of the Horniman's extraordinary 125th anniversary year."

The Nature Gallery will combine more than 2,300 objects from the Horniman's collection, including its famously overstuffed walrus, as well as artist commissions and multisensory activities.

These include a ceiling projection showcasing life on the planet, a display on plastic pollution by a Deptford school and a hands-on nature discovery zone focused on local wildlife.

The museum said the gallery explored human connection to and reliance on nature, stories of extinction and climate change, and ideas about how people can shape the planet's future.

It is one of a number of developments at the Horniman as part of its Nature + Love project, and is being supported by a £30,000 crowdfunding campaign, which has raised more than £14,000 to date.

Stuart McLeod, from The National Lottery Heritage Fund, said they were proud to support the project.

"It will help people of all ages connect with nature, understand the challenges it faces today and be inspired to play their part in protecting it," he said.

Arts minister Ruth Mackenzie added that she was "delighted" to have supported the refurbishment with £1.4m in infrastructure funding.

Gordon Seabright, chief executive at the Horniman, said: "We can't wait for these new spaces to be open so we can welcome everyone to share the wonder and beauty of nature."

The project was also funded by the Wolfson Foundation, Kusuma Trust, Garfield Weston Foundation, the Foyle Foundation and other donors.

articles.title: A UK collector paid £15 for a broken, lidless teapot at a 2016 auction; experts identified it as one of only seven known John Bartlam pieces, and it sold for £575,000 to The Met in New York
articles.summary: A UK collector who paid just £15 for a broken, lidless teapot at an auction in 2016 later discovered that the piece was one of the rarest known examples
articles.body: A UK collector who paid just £15 for a broken, lidless teapot at an auction in 2016 later discovered that the piece was one of the rarest known examples of early American porcelain. The teapot was eventually sold for £575,000, after experts identified it as a piece made by Staffordshire potter John Bartlam in South Carolina in the 1760s.The collector, a private buyer from south-west England, had bought the teapot at a general auction in the Midlands, The Independent reported. It had a broken handle and was missing its lid. At the time, the piece was thought to be Isleworth pottery, made at a factory in Middlesex between 1766 and 1800. However, the buyer was not convinced by that identification.He then took the teapot to Clare Dunham, an expert at Woolley and Wallis auctioneers in Salisbury. Its blue and white decoration, including a distinctive palm tree design, led Dunham to identify it as the work of John Bartlam. Bartlam had left England around 1763 and established a pottery business in South Carolina.The identification changed the significance of the damaged teapot. Experts said it was only the seventh recorded piece of Bartlam porcelain to have reached the market and the only known Bartlam teapot. This made it the earliest American-manufactured teapot to have been discovered.The teapot was then put up for auction by Woolley and Wallis. It was given an estimate of £10,000 to £20,000, while The Independent reported that it was expected to reach as much as £50,000. Instead, bidding pushed the price much higher, with the hammer falling at £460,000.After the buyer’s premium and fees were added, the teapot sold for £575,000. It was bought by London dealer Rod Jellicoe, who was bidding on behalf of The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.How the teapot was identifiedThe teapot had several features that helped connect it to Bartlam’s pottery. Woolley and Wallis described it as a previously unrecorded American porcelain teapot attributed to John Bartlam and dated it to around 1765–69.The auction house said it was made of porcelain with underglaze blue decoration. One side showed two cranes beneath a tall palm tree, with figures in a sampan and another figure in a separate boat. The other side featured a version of the Man on the Bridge pattern, showing a bridge connecting small islands in a Chinese pagoda landscape.The teapot was about 9cm high and 17.5cm across. Its cover was missing, while the handle had broken off and been restuck.Woolley and Wallis said the teapot had only recently been identified as an example of early American porcelain. It was believed to have been part of a matched tea service that reached England in the late 1760s or 1770s.The auction house also linked the teapot to other pieces associated with Bartlam’s pottery. Four teabowls from the same group had been found to match pieces of pottery excavated at Bartlam’s factory site in Cain Hoy, South Carolina.The teapot was one of only seven recorded pieces of Bartlam porcelain at the time. The other known pieces included four teabowls and two saucers from the same set.John Bartlam and his South Carolina potteryBartlam was trained in Staffordshire, England, and moved to South Carolina around 1763. He established his pottery at Cain Hoy, outside Charleston, with the aim of producing porcelain in America rather than relying on luxury porcelain imported from England.The Met says the teapot was made at Bartlam’s pottery in Cain Hoy around 1765–69. It describes the object as soft-paste porcelain with underglaze blue decoration.The pottery was established at a time when deposits of the special clay needed to make porcelain had recently been discovered in the Carolinas. The clay was being mined and shipped from Charleston to England.Bartlam wanted his business to compete with the luxury porcelain being produced in England and sent to the American colonies. His work therefore represented an attempt to produce similar goods in the colonies.The Met’s records also note that Josiah Wedgwood was concerned about the competition. In a 1767 letter to Thomas Bentley, Wedgwood referred to a “Pottwork in Charles Town” that was using Cherokee clay from the Carolinas to make porcelain.Research and archaeological excavations in the early 1990s later provided evidence of a porcelain factory at Cain Hoy dating to the late 1760s. According to The Met, the factory predates the American China Manufactory established by Gousse Bonnin and George Anthony Morris in Philadelphia in 1770.Why the teapot is significantThe teapot is now part of The Metropolitan Museum of Art’s collection and is on view at The Met Fifth Avenue in Gallery 723. The museum identifies John Bartlam as its manufacturer and dates it to around 1765–69.The Met says the object is one of only seven examples that can be associated with Bartlam’s factory. All seven are teawares and feature the palmetto, a motif not found in English porcelains. The palmetto is the state tree of South Carolina and provides a direct connection to the teapot’s American origin.The museum also notes that the teapot has a very white porcelain body and is thinly potted. Its decoration includes landscape scenes in the chinoiserie style, a style that reflected the popularity of Asian-inspired designs in European porcelain at the time.For the collector who originally bought the damaged piece, the discovery was unexpected. He said he had spent decades studying ceramics but had never expected to find such a rare object. “I have been studying ceramics for 30 years and I never dreamt that I would find such a rarity as this teapot,” he said as qouted by The Independent.He also said he was pleased not only with the auction result but with where the teapot would eventually go. “Not only am I extremely pleased for the result for myself, but also because the teapot is going home to America where it will be on public display for generations to come.“I spent a lot of time in the ceramic galleries at the Victoria and Albert Museum when I was first learning about ceramics and just never thought that one day I would have a hand in providing a major museum with such a unique and wonderful object”.Woolley and Wallis said the teapot had “caught the imagination of many” and that it was “absolutely delighted” with the sale.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk: Department of War revenue for my companies is …
articles.summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey recently pushed back against a report that said two major US defence contractors would help lead a Pentagon project that
articles.body: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey recently pushed back against a report that said two major US defence contractors would help lead a Pentagon project that could benefit them. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Palmer Luckey said he is advising the project in a personal capacity and rejected the description of Anduril as one of the US Department of Defense's biggest contractors. The post soon caught the attention of Tesla CEO Elon Musk who replied to Luckey's post, saying government defence revenue makes up only a small part of the total revenue of his companies.“Dept of War revenue for my companies is close to a rounding error of total revenue. Probably around 3% of SpaceX’s December ARR and ~1% of all my companies combined,” Elon Musk said.Palmer Luckey says he is 'not representing Anduril'In the X post, Palmer Luckey was responding to a Politico report about Project Meridian, a Pentagon initiative looking at how warfare could change in the future. “Why are you lying?” Luckey wrote in his post adding “I am not Anduril, I am advising in a personal capacity.”Luckey also challenged the report's description of Anduril as one of the Department of Defense's biggest contractors. “Even if this was an Anduril project, it is nuts to call 67th place one of the Department's biggest contractors.”He said the ranking was clear and questioned why the report had presented the information that way. “You know this isn't true, but presumably you start your story with this false claim for a reason.”In the post, Luckey also shared a table showing defence contractor revenue rankings in his X post. The table showed companies such as Lockheed Martin and RTX among the biggest defence contractors, while Anduril was ranked much lower. Luckey used the ranking to support his argument that describing Anduril as one of the Pentagon's biggest contractors was misleading.What is Pentagon's Project MeridianProject Meridian is aimed at studying possible changes in future warfare. The project is linked to a commission led by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, with input from people including Palmer Luckey, Elon Musk and Newt Gingrich. The commission is expected to study future military and warfare trends and produce a report by January 2027.The project has raised concerns about whether people advising the Pentagon could benefit from future defence contracts.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Who is safe?' Delhi minister Sirsa attacks Punjab govt after Mad Sandhu killing
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Saturday hit out at the Punjab government over the killing of makeup artist and social
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Saturday hit out at the Punjab government over the killing of makeup artist and social media influencer Mad Sandhu, alleging that the state’s law and order was in the hands of the “mafia”.Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Police said the attackers opened fire before fleeing the spot.Sandhu suffered two gunshot wounds and was rushed to a private hospital in critical condition, where he later died during treatment. An eyewitness said around two to three rounds were fired and that Sandhu was shot at close range.Reacting to the killing, Sirsa questioned the law and order situation in Punjab and alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.“There is no law and order in Punjab. The law and order situation in Punjab is in the hands of the mafia. In Punjab, you receive only one piece of information every day,” Sirsa told ANI.“Otherwise, the police do not even register an FIR. If they are drug dealers, they are going around killing people. If they are mafia members, they are killing people. If there are gangsters, they are killing people. Social media influencer Mad Sandhu was shot dead and if even the Sarpanch of a village is not safe, and a former Sarpanch is not safe, then who is safe?”Sirsa further alleged that extortion gangs, mafia groups and the drug mafia were operating in Punjab. “During the tenure of the Aam Aadmi Party, gangs involved in extortion, the mafia, and the drug mafia are operating in Punjab. There is also a school mafia operating, where even if you raise your voice against problems in schools, you will be thrown out of the party,” he added.Who was Mad Sandhu?Madhusudan Sandhu was a makeup artist and social media influencer who regularly appeared on podcasts and digital platforms, where he spoke about make-up artistry, the film industry and gender issues. His content and fashion choices had also attracted criticism and abuse on social media.Sandhu had around 2.26 lakh followers on Instagram and had acted in the Punjabi film *Oye Bhole Oye*. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh had objected to his social media content and clothing, saying his videos could have a negative impact on young people.Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka also criticised the AAP government over the killing and demanded Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation, alleging that the government had failed to protect people.Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them publicly on social media. He questioned why the threats had not been taken seriously and demanded an early arrest and a thorough investigation into who was behind the killing and why Sandhu had been threatened.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: AAP holds protest after 3 women journalists allege sexual harassment by cops - key points
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Three women journalists have alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three women journalists have alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3, with the complaints now transferred to the Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial enquiry”. The allegations have drawn criticism from journalists and opposition leaders, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CJP) set to protest over the incident.AAP Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj and party workers staged protests in front of Parliament Street police station, demanding registration of an FIR.The complaints were received by the New Delhi district police following the protest, during which police personnel were deployed to maintain law and order. Delhi Police said the complaints against police officers were being transferred to the Crime Branch, Kamla Market, which will examine the allegations and record statements of the complainants and other people concerned.The allegations have also triggered wider questions over the treatment of journalists and protesters during the demonstrations. CJP has announced a protest following the allegations, while journalist Dipke hit out at Delhi Police on X, alleging that the force had also picked up people who had no connection with CJP and tried to link them to the organisation to establish a foreign-funding angle.What the journalists allegedOne of the journalists told PTI that an assistant commissioner of police sexually assaulted her while she was covering the protest. She alleged that police personnel were detaining protesters and that no women police personnel were present at the spot."Police personnel were detaining protesters, and there were no women police personnel present at the spot. I asked ACP Vivek Bhagat of the Delhi Police about the absence of women police personnel, following which he sexually assaulted me and pushed me back," she alleged.The journalist said she and others subsequently went to a police station to lodge an FIR but alleged that no action had been taken so far. Delhi Police, however, said on Sunday that complaints had been received from three women journalists alleging sexual harassment by police personnel."On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints," Delhi Police informed on X.Dipke's allegations, Rahul Gandhi's attackDipke alleged that Delhi Police had also detained people who had nothing to do with CJP and tried to establish a foreign-funding connection."Delhi Police has also picked up a couple of people who had nothing to do with CJP and tried to forcibly link them to CJP to establish a foreign-funding angle. A friend just told me that one of them was brutally beaten by Delhi Police and has also lost his job because of the arrest," Dipke wrote on X.The Press Council of India expressed “shock and dismay” over the treatment of journalists and urged Delhi Police to immediately act on the complaint.Rahul Gandhi also accused Delhi Police of misconduct at Jantar Mantar and questioned Union home minister Amit Shah over the alleged treatment of journalists and protesters.The protests were held against CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid demonstrations over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Delhi Police detained several protesters, while at least three FIRs were registered in connection with the mass protest held near Jantar Mantar on October 2.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
